Standard: The engine completely contains a fan, compressor or turbine blade failure. No uncontained fires, or leakage of flammable fluid result and the engine contains all parts damaged and released by the failure of a single blade. Uncontained failures will not cause fire or catastrophic damage to engine external systems or air vehicle systems, or injury to personnel. “Single blade” is defined consistent with 7.3.12 criteria: a. For conventional blades, fracture in the blade attachments at the minimum neck section above the outermost retention feature. b. For integrally bladed rotors, fracture at the outer tangency point of the blade root fillet or, for welded or bonded airfoils, at the bond plane. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examine drawings or system configuration descriptions to verify that external engine and air vehicle systems (e.g., fuel, hydraulic lines) are routed to reduce exposure and limit secondary damage. Analysis.
  (1) Blade containment analysis which relates the released blade kinetic energy to the energy required for containment is accomplished for each rotor stage.
  (2) For uncontained failures, trade studies and failure risk assessments (e.g., FMECA, SSHA) are accomplished jointly with the airframer to substantiate containment strategy decisions. Test.
    (1) Lab test: The analysis is substantiated or correlated with rig or full engine containment tests of the most limiting stage in a ground-based sea level test cell.
